Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 1
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a factual error regarding cell biology by incorrectly identifying the "cell wall" as the most reliable major difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells in the context of standard diagrams. While many prokaryotes have cell walls, many eukaryotes (like animal cells) do not, making the cell wall an inconsistent differentiator. Conversely, the presence of a membrane-bound nucleus is the defining, universal characteristic that distinguishes eukaryotic cells from prokaryotic cells. The Planner's reasoning ("Prokaryotes have a cell wall, while eukaryotes typically do not") is factually flawed because it ignores the vast number of eukaryotic cells that possess cell walls (plants, fungi, algae), leading to the selection of the wrong answer choice (C) instead of the correct one (B).
